scope: Context compression and its internal reviews
default_for_new_runs: parallel_v3 in Python, CLI and Workbench: the faithfulness review runs in parts and the global conflict review runs alongside both branches; CTXCOMP_CONTEXT_REVIEW_MODE selects another mode
historical_compatibility: Existing run inputs are unchanged. Explicit legacy mode is retained for historical authored-response replay.

wiring.after_both: context_conflicts in parallel_v1 and parallel_v2; parallel_v3 starts it alongside both branches
wiring.provider: One fresh isolated model call per pending role; exact validated same-run branch results may be reused on an explicit retry. New Codex calls use a new temporary directory and --ephemeral.
wiring.validation: ctxcomp.split_review.validate_branch runs on each response before aggregation.
wiring.release: Aggregate all three decisions and verify the branch proof before publishing main.json.

checks: field and atomic-claim coverage
exact source and candidate citations
evidence status consistency
stale response rejection
false PASS rejection
requirement and component coverage
source-unit coverage, including inventory omissions; from compression rules 1.20.0 only the proposal's units, with cited supporting passages checked where cited (tests/test_supporting_scope.py)
traceable target spans
mandatory requirements cannot become optional advice
false PASS rejection
all five global checks exactly once
source and candidate provenance
each unresolved global check blocks publication
neither prior branch may be overridden

limitations: Authored findings test validators and release gates, not whether an LLM detects semantic defects.
Provider wiring tests construct the real CLI adapter calls but stub their remote responses; no live external calls are made.
Exact quotation matching does not prove entailment, complete scientific coverage or human predictive validity.
Retry tests measure call counts using authored responses; real-provider speed and semantic accuracy have not been measured.

checks: A failed global call requires only one new call when both prior branches remain valid.
An invalid branch reruns without repeating its valid sibling.
Changed candidate, rules, schema, executor or validator code prevents reuse.
Changed prerequisite findings change the global-review request.
Altered cached artifacts stop execution.
An unchanged semantic failure is reused as failure, never resampled for PASS.
Custom adapters without explicit executor identity do not reuse reviews.
